title: Margaritas and Murder at El Paso: The Last Toast
venue: El Paso Mexican Restaurant — Denham Springs
series_title: Margaritas and Murder at El Paso

title_screen.subtitle: A Live Detective Mystery Experience
title_screen.hook: A private celebration ends with one final toast, a vanished sample bottle, and a manager too eager to blame an outside vendor.

truth.victim: Elena Cruz, private party guest of honor
truth.motive: Elena was about to reveal the manager's under-the-table event deposits and fake vendor invoices
truth.method: A private toast was switched with a mezcal sample containing a fast-acting toxin
truth.strongest_evidence: The vendor invoice number on the fake mezcal sample matches the manager's private event deposit ledger
truth.red_herring: The produce vendor's missing delivery receipt

briefing.host_read: Tonight at El Paso, dinner service turns into a crime scene. The salsa music is still playing, the patio lights are still warm, and every suspect has a reason to protect their own version of the night. Detectives, follow the receipts, the hallway timing, the patio noise, and what the staff tried to clean up before anyone called for help.
briefing.player_prompt: Review each app as clues unlock. Use the round checkpoints to organize what the evidence actually proves. Do not accuse on gossip alone.

clue_theme: private room service timeline, fake vendor invoices, toast glass switch, deposit ledger

0.public: Elena Cruz dies after a private-room toast. The manager immediately blames a vendor sample bottle that no one can find.

entries.title: Briefing Note
entries.content: Elena had requested a private conversation with management before the toast.

300.public: The private room timeline is crowded, but the toast service was controlled by fewer people than it first appears.

entries.title: Private Room Path
entries.content: Server entrance, office hallway, and bar pass form a tight triangle.

entries.title: Toast Setup
entries.content: Elena's glass is nearest the service tray edge in the first photo, then moved inward in the second.

600.public: The missing produce receipt is real, but vegetables did not touch the toast glass.

entries.title: Delivery Gap
entries.content: Produce vendor invoice missing signature, but delivery ended before the private party arrived.

900.public: Elena was not investigating food quality. She was investigating private event money.

entries.title: Private Deposit Pattern
entries.content: Several event deposits bypass normal register notes.

entries.title: Elena Text
entries.content: I have the invoices. We talk tonight.

1200.public: A fake mezcal sample gives the killer a clean excuse: blame the bottle, hide the switch.

entries.title: Vendor Lookup
entries.content: Sample distributor name does not match any active liquor vendor record.

1500.public: The strongest evidence is not the poison alone. It is the paperwork connecting the poison story to the money story.

entries.title: Ledger Fragment
entries.content: Private event deposit initials match manager approval marks.

entries.title: Vendor Contact
entries.content: Listed mezcal vendor number routes to a disposable phone.

1800.public: The last toast was staged to look imported, but the motive was inside the restaurant.

entries.title: Final Evidence
entries.content: Fake mezcal invoice number matches the manager's private event deposit ledger.

reveal_copy: The truth points to General Manager. The strongest case is not built on the loudest rumor, but on how motive, method, opportunity, and the evidence trail line up. The detail that closes it: The vendor invoice number on the fake mezcal sample matches the manager's private event deposit ledger.
